messages:
nina: FYI we have a new SAST/DAST correlated issue after the RBAC rename + KMS key rotation. Nightly pipeline surfaced a handful of findings that look like header logging and potential token exposure in staging. Opening thread to coordinate quick triage.

omar-scanner: Confirmed. DAST runner printed request headers when token fetch failed (debug mode). timestamp ~2026-03-10T00:22:10Z. I captured the log id: log-20260310-0022.

irene-infra: Context: RBAC rename svc/dast-runner -> svc/dast-scan at 2026-03-09T21:30Z. KMS rotation for staging happened at 2026-03-09T20:50Z. Could be a timing window where the token provider errored and fallback logic logged headers.

logbot: CI-SCAN: run-1299 flagged new SAST alerts in infra/dast/* (4 findings). See https://ci.example/jobs/1299.

chris-sre: Immediate steps: (1) revoke any staging tokens associated with the scanner, (2) flip scanner to unauthenticated for staging, (3) add a temporary log pipeline rule to mask Authorization headers so existing logs don't leak into analytics.

nina: I agree. Also we need an evidence snapshot before we redact anything for compliance. We should tar and hash the artifacts and upload to secure storage.

omar-scanner: Revoke done. Disabled auth in staging config and restarted canary. Also opened PR to remove debug header logging: https://git.example/infra/dast/pull/110. Patch replaces direct header logging with redaction middleware.

irene-infra: I'll run the audit reconstruction to map old->new principals so compliance has a consistent view. Plan: query logs for principal names matching svc/dast-* between 2026-03-09T20:00Z and 2026-03-10T01:00Z, create CSV with (ts, original_principal, canonical_principal, resource, action, log_id). Command: `gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:"svc/dast-*"' --start=2026-03-09T20:00:00Z --end=2026-03-10T01:00:00Z --format json > /tmp/dast-principals.json` then run mapping script.

sec-oncall: Please create INC-2026-052 and attach timeline. Evidence requirements: raw logs, tar.gz, sha256 HMAC using team HMAC_KEY, and manifest.json with canonical mapping. No public disclosure.

chris-sre: For short-term log masking, I'll add a Fluent Bit filter that replaces `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with `Authorization: [REDACTED]`. Example sed: `s/(Authorization:\s*)Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/\1[REDACTED]/g`. Will coordinate with logging team to apply to staging index.

omar-scanner: Note: the scanner container id was dast-runner-7b4f. When I grepped logs I also found two outbound connections to 35.212.11.9 at 2026-03-09T23:12Z (likely telemetry). I'll post the raw egress IP list after further triage.

nina: Good catch. If egress hosts are not in approved list, escalate immediately. Benign telemetry hosts must be whitelisted and documented.

irene-infra: Mapping script done. Output CSV uploaded to s3://redwood-sec/incidents/INC-2026-052/evidence/mapping-3481239999.csv. Creating evidence archive now: `tar czf evidence-3481239999.tar.gz /tmp/dast-logs /tmp/mapping-3481239999.csv` then `aws s3 cp evidence-3481239999.tar.gz s3://redwood-sec/incidents/INC-2026-052/`.

sec-oncall: When you upload, compute HMAC: `openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$HMAC_KEY" -binary evidence-3481239999.tar.gz | base64 > evidence-3481239999.hmac` and attach both to the incident.

omar-scanner: PR merged to remove header logging and to default `auth.enabled=false` for staging config. Also added unit test that simulates an auth failure and asserts logs do not contain Bearer token.

chris-sre: Masking filter applied to staging logging pipeline. Old logs will be re-indexed with a redaction pass where feasible, but the original archive is preserved per sec-oncall request.

nina: SAST re-run queued on hotfix branch. If we still see similar patterns elsewhere, escalate to SRE and mark high.

logbot: CI re-run 1301: SAST scan on hotfix branch — status: PASS (no new header-logging findings).

irene-infra: Uploaded evidence archive and HMAC to S3 and attached links in INC-2026-052. Also added canonical mapping CSV and a short README explaining the RBAC rename and transform rules.

sec-oncall: Thanks. Schedule 60-min postmortem tomorrow 09:00-10:00; include infra, scanner, SRE, and audit. Postmortem should include timeline, root cause (race during KMS rotation + RBAC rename), remediation, and action items: CI gate for secret availability, logging hardening, and detection alert on Authorization header occurrences.

chris-sre: I'll file follow-ups: LOG-210 (pipeline masking), CI-812 (pre-scan secret presence check), SAST-499 (rule to flag header-logging patterns).

nina: Closing thread unless new evidence surfaces. Great teamwork. :white_check_mark:
